review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for Mathlib counterparts to `augmentationIdeal`, `squareZeroQuotientEquiv`, `squareZeroQuotientMap` and the cotangent equivalences. The only Mathlib augmentation material is the predicate `Ideal.IsAugmentation` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/IsAugmentation.lean. It is a different concept: it is a complement condition on an ideal, not a named ideal. `augmentationIdeal` is just `RingHom.ker` of `algebraMapInv`. Mathlib has the same kernel only as an unnamed `RingHom.ker`. The `counitAlgHom` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/SymmetricAlgebra.lean is `algebraMapInv` by `rfl`, so `augmentationIdeal` is a small named wrapper and not a competing concept. Mathlib has no symmetric-algebra-to-`TrivSqZeroExt` comparison. A grep of Mathlib's TrivSqZeroExt, Cotangent and Kaehler files found no `SymmetricAlgebra` content there. The equivalences here use existing Mathlib operations: `Ideal.cotangentEquivIdeal`, `TrivSqZeroExt.kerIdeal`, `TrivSqZeroExt.map` and `Ideal.quotientMapₐ`. Remaining uncertainty: I did not search the other Formal Frontier libraries beyond a file-name search for `augmentationIdeal` and `squareZeroQuotient`. That search found only this library's own tests and docs, plus one unrelated algebraic-groups test file with no SymmetricAlgebra or TrivSqZeroExt content.
